name: Hearthstone Firearms Homestead-12 'Door Slam'
description:
The Hearthstone Homestead-12 is a pump-action shotgun chambered in 12 gauge with a five-round tubular magazine and an 18-inch barrel. It is the cheapest functional shotgun in GLMZ, manufactured with the same cost-conscious approach that defines Hearthstone's product line — stamped steel receiver, hardwood stock finished with lacquer rather than oil, and a bead front sight that serves as the only aiming reference.

The Door Slam is the Gray Zone home defense standard. Where the Guardian-12 pistol provides comfort, the Homestead provides capability — a 12-gauge shotgun loaded with buckshot is effective against nearly any unarmored threat at room distance, regardless of the shooter's training level. The pump action is simple to operate, visually intimidating when racked, and mechanically reliable in a way that budget semi-automatics cannot match.

Hearthstone sells the Homestead-12 with a box of twenty-five buckshot shells and a trigger lock. Their marketing acknowledges the weapon's real purpose without euphemism: 'When they come through the door, be on the other side of this.' The weapon sells by the tens of thousands annually and constitutes the backbone of the Gray Zone residential defense.
specifications:
caliber: 12 gauge
effective_range: 30 meters (buckshot)
rate_of_fire: Pump-action
magazine_capacity: 5+1 rounds
weight: 2.8 kg
tactical_use: A basic pump-action shotgun for home defense. The 12-gauge buckshot pattern at room distance covers approximately 25cm, providing a forgiving hit area for stressed shooters. The pump action is manually cycled, which prevents short-stroking malfunctions common in untrained users. Effective against unarmored targets at close range. Limited by tube-magazine capacity and slow reloading.
cultural_context: The Door Slam is the sound of the Gray Zone home defense — the distinctive racking of a pump shotgun is the most universally recognized warning sound in residential GLMZ. Families keep them behind doors and under beds. Community defense groups use them as their primary long arm. The Homestead-12 is not glamorous, but it is the weapon that protects more homes than any other.
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone block organizes a defense drill using Homestead-12s, and the corponation that owns the building sends a cease-and-desist. The residents' refusal to comply becomes a political flashpoint.
A modified Homestead-12 with an illegal extended magazine tube and pistol grip is found at every scene of a serial vigilante's work in a the Gray Zone district.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian pump-action shotgun with a distinctly no-nonsense aesthetic. Compact and stocky, built for close-quarters work rather than elegance. The receiver sits low and purposeful, the foregrip prominent for the characteristic pump cycling motion. Silhouette reads as purely functional—honest industrial design.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length 97 cm, barrel 45.7 cm, receiver width 5.2 cm. Tubular magazine runs beneath the barrel from muzzle to trigger guard.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but manageable—2.8 kg settles firmly in the hands with reassuring mechanical solidity. Feels built to absorb recoil and punishment rather than impress with balance.
physical_description.primary_material: Stamped steel receiver and barrel, cost-conscious manufacturing evident in the fabrication method rather than material weakness. Hardwood furniture—real lacquered wood, not polymer substitutes.
physical_description.finish: Matte blued steel with light surface oxidation patterns suggesting honest use. Lacquered hardwood with visible grain, finish slightly worn at edges from handling. Bead front sight catches light like a dull pearl.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray-blue receiver and barrel contrasted with warm tan-brown lacquered hardwood stock and foregrip. Minimal contrast intentional—designed to be noticed, not admired.
physical_description.grip_texture: Lacquered hardwood stock with subtle grain texture, slightly slick from repeated hand oils. Pump foregrip wrapped in scored hardwood, deeply grooved for secure manipulation under stress.
distinctive_features: Single bead front sight mounted on barrel—only aiming reference
Tubular magazine tube with cross-pin retention visible beneath barrel
Pump lever with deliberate mechanical feedback
Trigger guard with functional geometry, no aesthetic flourish
Muzzle crown shows simple machining lines
Factory trigger lock installed through trigger guard
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: "HEARTHSTONE FIREARMS" stamped in simple block letters on left side of receiver. Serial number stamped into steel below the markings. Minimal branding—manufacturer's confidence expressed through restraint.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained within economic constraints. Finish shows honest wear from regular handling and maintenance cycles. No cosmetic damage, but patina develops naturally from use. This is a working tool that ages gracefully through function.
